source.title: Why Small Delays Change Large Systems

content.title: Why Small Delays Change Large Systems

paragraphs.text: Complex systems often look stable until feedback arrives too late. A small delay between an action and its visible consequence can make people repeat the action, creating a much larger response than they intended.
The important lesson is not that delay is always harmful. It is that decisions improve when the delay is made explicit, measured, and considered before another intervention is added.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why can a small delay produce a large response?

options.A: Because delayed feedback can lead people to repeat an action before seeing its effect.
options.B: Because complex systems always reject early interventions.
options.C: Because visible consequences are usually unrelated to previous actions.
options.D: Because measuring a delay automatically removes it.

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the second paragraph?

options.A: Every delayed outcome should be treated as a failure.
options.B: Good decisions account for delay before adding another intervention.
options.C: Complex systems should be changed as quickly as possible.
options.D: Measurement is less useful than intuition.
